newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to ease car imports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to ease car imports.

text.p: Turkey is studying a plan to ease car imports by Turkish workers abroad who hold savings at the Turkish central bank for one year in a move to raise funds to help bridge gaping deficits, officials said on Friday.

They said workers in Europe, numbering about three million, would be able to bring cars with an age of maximum four years into Turkey without customs duties if they deposit at least 50,000 marks for one year at the central bank, according to the regulation.
Under the present import regime, cars with a maximum age of three years can be imported by paying custom duties.
The workers would also benefit from a 20 percent tax discount when they sell the cars they imported.
The regulation aims at attracting foreign currency from cash-rich Turkish workers abroad, mainly in Germany, who generally deposit their savings in German banks or buy estate in Turkey.
But the government move was sharply criticised by the automobile industry, a key sector in the country, and trade unions which represent some 400,000 workers in the sector in total.
"This will be a serious blow to the automobile sector," said Inan Kirac, a senior executive from Koc Holding which is the top car producer in Turkey with licences from Italian Fiat.
"If the law is passed, about 120,000 workers from the car plants will be redundant," he was quoted as saying by the state Anatolian news agency. "Turkey will turn into a junkyard of European cars."
Officials did not say how much the scheme, part of a series of government measures to find resources to close trade and budget deficits, was planned to raise.
Kirac said the regulation would also violate Turkey's customs union agreement with the European Union which annulled customs duties mutually in many industrial goods and took effect in January.
"Car imports are exempt from the customs agreement," he said.
Turkish residents will not benefit from the regulation, to be effective until the end of this year if approved.

The automobile sector employs about 400,000 workers in 16 production plants and nearly 500 spare part sub-contractors. There are 25 car importers in Turkey which bring in major European, Japanese and American products.

The Association of Automobile Industrialists said on Friday 120,173 cars were sold in Turkey in the first seven months of 1996, including 24,112 imported cars, compared to 110,295 cars, including 8,040 imported ones, in January-July 1995.
The share of imported cars in the domestic market almost tripled to 20 percent over the same period.
